0.headline: Steamhouse India to open Rs 414-crore IPO on September 9
0.heading: Steamhouse India to open Rs 414-crore IPO on September 9
0.intro: Steamhouse India is raising Rs 353 crore through a fresh issue of shares, while promoter Vishal Sanwarprasad Budhia will offload shares worth Rs 61 crore through an offer for sale.
0.body:
Gujarat-based industrial gas supplier Steamhouse India is set to launch its Rs 414-crore IPO for public subscription on September 9, becoming the 11th company in the mainboard segment to hit Dalal Street next week.

Pranav Constructions, Arcil, Rentomojo, Karamtara Engineering, LCC Projects, Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions, Kanohar Electricals, Nuvama Wealth Management, Glass Wall Systems (India) and Veegaland Developers are the other 10 companies scheduled to open their IPOs next week. The 11 companies are collectively looking to raise Rs 7,054 crore.

Steamhouse India is raising Rs 353 crore through a fresh issue of shares, while promoter Vishal Sanwarprasad Budhia will offload shares worth Rs 61 crore through an offer for sale.

Before filing its red herring prospectus, the company undertook a pre-IPO placement of equity shares worth nearly Rs 50 crore. Accordingly, the amount raised through the pre-IPO round was deducted from the fresh issue size.

The anchor book will open for a day on September 8, while the IPO will remain open for public subscription until September 11. The share allotment is expected to be finalised by September 15, with the company's shares scheduled to list on the stock exchanges on September 17.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Steamhouse India specialises in the generation and centralised distribution of industrial gases, including steam and nitrogen, through its pipeline network. It is the only company in India that supplies nitrogen through a distributed pipeline network, instead of the more common practice of supplying it in cryogenic tanks or through onsite nitrogen generation.

Of the net proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 180 crore will be utilised to repay debt, against total borrowings of Rs 400.2 crore as of July 2026.

A further Rs 75.9 crore will be used to expand the capacity of its Ankleshwar and Panoli facilities, while Rs 38.1 crore will be spent on setting up a new steam-generation facility at Dahej GIDC. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Steamhouse India has an established industrial customer base in Gujarat, including Aether Industries, Anupam Rasayan India, Globe Enviro Care, Gujarat Polysol Chemicals, Devanshi Dyestuff, Mahavir Synthesis, Mangalam Intermediaries and Subhasri Pigments.

In fiscal 2026, revenue from repeat customers accounted for 90.72 percent of the company's revenue from operations.

The company's profit for the year ended March 2026 rose 24 percent to Rs 38.6 crore from Rs 31.2 crore in the previous year. Revenue from operations increased 24.4 percent to Rs 491.5 crore from Rs 395.1 crore during the same period.

Equirus Capital has been appointed as the book-running lead manager for the Steamhouse India IPO.

1.headline: Pranav Constructions raises Rs 84.2 crore from anchor investors ahead of Rs 351-crore IPO
1.heading: Pranav Constructions raises Rs 84.2 crore from anchor investors ahead of Rs 351-crore IPO
1.intro: Pranav Constructions IPO | The company will open its Rs 351-crore public issue for public subscription on September 7 and close the issue on September 9.
1.body:
Mumbai-based real estate developer Pranav Constructions has raised Rs 84.2 crore from nine anchor investors, including Goldman Sachs, ITI Mutual Fund and Taurus Mutual Fund, on September 4, a day ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO).

The company will open its Rs 351-crore IPO for public subscription on September 7 and close the issue on September 9. The price band has been fixed at Rs 118-124 per share.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 315.6 crore, while existing investor BioUrja India Infra will offer 28.56 lakh shares worth Rs 35.42 crore through an offer for sale.

Pranav Constructions, promoted by Pranav Kiran Ashar and Ravi Ramalingam, on Friday allotted 67.94 lakh equity shares to anchor investors at the upper end of the price band.

Goldman Sachs Investments (Mauritius) emerged as the largest investor in the anchor book, acquiring 20.16 lakh shares for Rs 25 crore.

Of the total anchor allocation, 19.75 lakh equity shares were allotted to two domestic mutual funds — ITI Mutual Fund and Taurus Mutual Fund — which participated through a total of seven schemes.

Other investors that participated in the anchor book included Abudantia Capital, Ashika India Select Fund, Asio Fund, Rigel Global Fund and Saint Capital Fund.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Pranav Constructions plans to utilise Rs 145.7 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue to fund redevelopment expenses, while Rs 91.5 crore will be used for debt repayment. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

According to the company, the redevelopment expenses include costs related to obtaining government and statutory approvals, purchasing additional floor space index (FSI), and compensating members for alternate accommodation and hardship compensation in connection with certain under-construction and upcoming redevelopment projects.

The company operates primarily in the Mumbai suburban region and has a portfolio of 65 redevelopment projects across the MCGM region. This includes 28 completed projects, 20 under-construction projects with a total developable area of 1.63 million square feet, and 17 upcoming projects with a total developable area of 1.96 million square feet.

On the financial front, Pranav Constructions reported a profit of Rs 71.3 crore for the fiscal year ended March 2026, up 14.6 percent from Rs 62.3 crore in the previous fiscal year. Revenue increased 19.7 percent to Rs 761.6 crore from Rs 636.3 crore during the same period.

Centrum Broking and PNB Investment Services are acting as the merchant bankers to the public issue.

2.headline: IPO rush ahead? Over 30 issuers face September 30 SEBI approval deadline
2.heading: IPO rush ahead? Over 30 issuers face September 30 SEBI approval deadline
2.intro: Over 30 issuers are rushing to launch IPOs before SEBI approvals expire on September 30
2.body:
Over 30 issuers are looking to make their way to the public markets before their observation from SEBI expires on September 30.

Given the geopolitical turmoil earlier this year, the market sentiment was extremely weak, resulting in firms delaying their plans to list on the bourses. However, the regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) released a circular allowing IPO approvals that expire between April 1 and September 30, 2026 to remain valid till September 30, 2026.

This gave companies around 6-month additional time to launch public issues without having to restart the regulatory process. Under the normal route observation letter is valid for 12 months and, if filed through confidential route validity is up to 18 months.

However, with the September 30th deadline fast approaching, investment bankers and issuers are gearing up for a rush of firms making their way to the markets.

Of the issuers that will see their approval expire, a significant portion are likely to aim to list before the deadline. However, there are some firms that are likely to see their approval expire and re-attempt their way to the bourses during better market conditions.

Speaking on the condition of anonymity, a banker of one of the IPOs said, "Those who need to raise capital will come to markets, because they need the money. However, those who have a larger OFS component can put it off as exit liquidity can come later as well."



Further, the financial statements included in an offer document cannot be more than six months old. "Accordingly, issuers seeking to launch their IPOs on the basis of their audited financial statements for fiscal 2026 would generally need to do so by September 30, failing which updated financial information would be required," explained Richa Choudhary, Partner - Capital Markets, Trilegal.

"The convergence of these two timelines naturally creates a rush among issuers to access the markets before the end of September," she added.

If the observation letter expires, firms will be forced to refile their issue, which will lead them to redo a substantial part of the IPO process.

In a refiling, a firm will have to prepare and file a fresh DRHP, update existing documentation, and undergo the regulator's review once again.  "The fresh filing would also need to appropriately incorporate and address the observations received during the earlier review process," Choudhary said.

Importantly, the refiling also requires an updated due diligence exercise covering developments since the previous filing. This involves additional work across the issuer, legal counsel, bankers, auditors and other intermediaries, and therefore has both significant timing and cost implications.
